data.narrative:
X-Bow Systems, a Series B defense and security technology company founded by Jason Hundley, Mark Kaufman, and Maureen Gannon, has raised $157M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comparable universe of 10 peers—2 public companies (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) and 8 private firms in the same sector and stage—including Dream Security, Harmattan AI, Code Metal, Castelion, and Defense Unicorns.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using total raised as a proxy baseline, applies a 1.9x multiplier typical of Series B advancement, yielding $298M. Peer-median methodology across 7 same-sector, same-stage comparables produces a $1.0B implied value, with a range spanning $300M to $3.0B. The peer set reflects material dispersion, with Dream Security valued at $3.0B against a lower quartile near $300M.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $254M (low), $649M (median), and $1.1B (high). The 4.3x spread between low and high reflects genuine uncertainty in stage-appropriate multiples within the defense sector. Key drivers of valuation within this range include relative positioning against peer growth and revenue profiles, customer concentration and contract durability, and technology differentiation versus established competitors. The gap between stage-progression and peer-median methodologies warrants further diligence into whether X-Bow's capital efficiency and commercial traction align with peer benchmarks.
